site generator

A static site builder
that speaks Fez.

fez static turns one source folder of Markdown, HTML, layouts and parts into one output folder of finished pages. Layouts and pages use the same template syntax as components, collections come from folder names, and the whole thing ships inside the Fez CLI with no extra parser dependency. This site is built with it.

What it is Configuration Templates CLI

01 / 04

What it is

A convention-based generator: a source folder in, a target folder out, and a handful of rules that decide how every file gets there.

source_dir · target_dir · one config file

One folder in, one folder out

The config file lives in the project root. source_dir holds layouts/, parts/ and root/; root/ mirrors the public site exactly. Everything renders into target_dir.

Both directories are always resolved, with web_src and web_build as defaults, so a project with no config file still builds.

fez-static.yaml
web_src/
|-- layouts/
|   |-- default.html
|   `-- post.html
|-- parts/
|   `-- header.html
`-- root/
    |-- [blogs]/
    |   |-- 2026-01-01-hello.md
    |   `-- 2026-01-02-second.html
    |-- css/site.css
    |-- fez/ui-card.fez
    |-- index.html
    `-- about.md
web_build/
root/about.md->web_build/about.html
non-page files under root keep their path and are copied unchanged

.md · .html · YAML front matter

Markdown and HTML pages share front matter

Every page may start with a YAML block. title, description, layout, permalink, draft, render and components have meaning to the builder; anything else is passed through as page.* for templates.

Markdown is converted with the native Bun renderer and its braces are never evaluated, so documented Fez templates stay literal. HTML pages are full Fez templates.

---
title: Hello, Fez
description: The first post.
layout: post
date: 2026-01-01
permalink: /blog/hello/
tags: [intro, fez]
draft: false
---

# Hello, Fez

This `{page.title}` stays literal in Markdown.
web_build/blog/hello/index.htmlpage.tags available to the layout
index.md becomes index.html; other pages keep their relative path with an .html extension

[name] directories · collections.name · index.yaml

Collections from folder names

A bracketed directory such as root/[blogs] is a collection. Its pages are exposed to every template as collections.blogs, sorted newest first, publish under blogs/ and produce blogs/index.yaml with the metadata of each entry.

A leading YYYY-MM-DD- in the file name supplies date and is stripped from the public path; a missing title falls back to the first heading. Assets inside the folder are copied but are not entries.

- title: Second post
  date: 2026-01-02
  url: /blogs/second.html
  href: blogs/second.html
  collection: blogs
  source_path: "[blogs]/2026-01-02-second.html"
- title: Hello, Fez
  date: 2026-01-01
  url: /blog/hello/
  href: blog/hello/
  collection: blogs
  source_path: "[blogs]/2026-01-01-hello.md"
collections.blogs[0].contentrendered HTML body for templates, kept out of the YAML
the changelog on this site is a [changelog] collection

staging directory · generated notice · doctor

Safe writes and honest output

A build renders into a staging directory and swaps it into target_dir only after every page succeeded; a failing build leaves the previous output untouched. Missing layouts or parts, output collisions, include cycles and unsafe paths are build errors, not warnings.

Every generated HTML, Fez and JavaScript file starts with a notice that names its source, so nobody edits the wrong copy.

<!-- generated from src: web_src/root/index.html | DO NOT EDIT OR READ THIS FILE -->
<!doctype html>
...
render errorprevious build kept, stage removed
fez static doctor validates the same render without publishing it

02 / 04

Configuration

One optional YAML or JSON file. fez static init writes it with every option documented and only the two required paths active.

fez-static.yaml · fez-static.json · config/

Where the config lives

The builder looks for fez-static.yaml, then fez-static.json, first in the project root and then in config/. The first match wins. Every path inside it is relative to the project root and must stay inside it.

./fez-static.yaml
./fez-static.json
./config/fez-static.yaml
./config/fez-static.json
no filedefaults apply: web_src -> web_build
the legacy target key is rejected with a pointer to target_dir

source_dir · target_dir

The two required paths

source_dir is the site folder with layouts/, parts/ and root/. target_dir receives the build and is replaced on every successful run, so keep it out of version control or, as this repository does, commit it on purpose.

source_dir: demo_src
target_dir: demo
demo_src/root/static.html->demo/static.html
neither may be the project root or contain the other

site.title · site.description · any key

Site values for templates

Everything under site is exposed to layouts, parts and HTML pages as site.*. Beyond title and description the keys are yours; this site keeps its script URL and the list of global components there, and the shared head part loops over them.

site:
  title: Fez
  description: JavaScript DOM components framework
  fez_url: fez.min.js
  components:
    - /site.fez
    - /fez/fez-control.fez
<script src={site.fez_url}>{#each site.components as c}
site.pages and site.collections are added by the builder at render time

site.base_url · site.relative_urls

Base-aware or relative URLs

Leave base_url unset and put <base href={page.base}> in the layout: url(path) then emits site-root-relative paths that work at /demo/ locally and /fez/demo/ on GitHub Pages with no change. Set base_url for absolute site paths instead, or relative_urls: true to make every emitted link page-relative.

# unset (default)      url("/css/site.css") -> css/site.css
# base_url: /docs      url("/css/site.css") -> /docs/css/site.css
# relative_urls: true  url("/css/site.css") -> ../css/site.css  (from blog/hello/)
page.basepage.hrefpage.url
doctor flags root-relative links that ignore a configured base_url

copy

Copy build artifacts into the site

The copy map brings files or whole directories from outside source_dir into the target. Keys are project-root-relative sources, values are target-relative destinations. A file maps to one exact path; a directory copies recursively. Copied bytes are unchanged and the sources are watched by dev.

copy:
  "dist/fez.min.js": "fez.min.js"
  "dist/fez.min.js.map": "fez.min.js.map"
  "public": "vendor"
symlinks.tmp. filespaths outside the projectfail the build
a copy that lands on a rendered page is reported as an output collision

collections.name.layout · collections.name.required

Collection defaults and required metadata

Per collection you may set the default layout for its entries and a required list of front matter keys. Page front matter still overrides the layout; fez static doctor checks the required keys against the final metadata, including inferred titles and file name dates.

collections:
  blogs:
    layout: post
    required: [title, description, date]
doctorblogs/2026-01-03-draft.md is missing required fields: description
draft: true pages are excluded until you pass --drafts

serve_root · serve_prefix

Development server helpers

Rarely needed. serve_root serves a parent directory as the document root so you can browse /demo/ next to other files, and serve_prefix mounts everything under a URL prefix to mimic project-pages hosting. Requests outside the prefix redirect into it.

serve_root: .
serve_prefix: /fez
site:
  base_url: /demo
http://127.0.0.1:3000/fez/demo/
both stay inside the project root

03 / 04

Templates

Layouts, parts and HTML pages use the Fez template compiler: expressions, conditionals, loops, plus two build-time directives.

layouts/default.html · layout: name · layout: false

Layouts that nest

A page without layout uses layouts/default.html (or default.md). layout: post picks another file, .html first then .md. A layout may declare its own parent in front matter, and {@content} marks where the page or child layout goes. layout: false emits the page bare.

---
layout: default
---
<article data-date={page.date}>
  <h1>{page.title}</h1>
  {@content}
</article>
default.html>post.html>page body
layout cycles and a missing layout fail the build

{@include "name.html"} · include.*

Parts with parameters

{@include "name.html"} inserts a file from parts/; it works in pages, layouts and other parts and may nest. Pass one object and read it as include.* inside the part. ./name.html resolves relative to the current part. Paths must be quoted literals so the build stays static.

<!-- layout -->
{@include "badge.html", { label: page.title, kind: "note" }}

<!-- parts/badge.html -->
<strong class={include.kind}>{include.label}</strong>
<strong class="note">Hello, Fez</strong>
include cycles and paths escaping parts/ are build errors

site · page · collections · include · url()

The render context

Every template sees site (config values plus all pages), page (front matter plus url, href, base, slug, date, collection), collections, include and the url(path) helper. The same {#if}, {#each} and {expression} syntax as in components applies.

<h1>{site.title}</h1>
<ul>
  {#each collections.blogs as post}
    <li>
      <a href={post.href}>{post.title}</a>
      {#if post.date}<time>{post.date}</time>{/if}
    </li>
  {/each}
</ul>
<script fez={url("/fez/ui-card.fez")}></script>
post.contentrendered Markdown body, ready for {@html}
script, style, pre, code and xmp regions are left untouched by the compiler

components: · .fez under root · Fez in the browser

Fez components on generated pages

A .fez file under root/ is published like any asset, with the generated notice on top. Pages list the components they need in front matter, and the shared head part loads site.components for every page plus page.components for the current one. The browser compiles them; the generator never does.

<script src={site.fez_url}></script>
{#each site.components as component}
  <script fez={url(component)}></script>
{/each}
{#each page.components as component}
  <script fez={url(component)}></script>
{/each}
site-navsite-liveui-editorthis page
the site navigation, footer and these code cards are Fez components

render: false · layout: false · permalink

Passthrough and custom routes

An existing complete HTML document can be published as-is with layout: false and render: false; it only gains the generated notice. permalink: /docs/start/ writes docs/start/index.html regardless of the source path, and draft: true hides a page until --drafts.

---
layout: false
render: false
permalink: /old/page/
---
<!doctype html>
<html>...</html>
web_build/old/page/index.htmlbyte-for-byte body, notice on line one
two pages resolving to the same output path is a build error

04 / 04

CLI

Six commands and four options. fez static alone is build; every command accepts an optional project root as its only positional argument.

fez static init

Start from a documented config

Creates fez-static.yaml with every option written out as a comment and only source_dir and target_dir active, plus a layout, a home page, two collection posts and a stylesheet. It refuses to overwrite an existing site, and honours an existing config's source_dir.

Created ./web_src with 6 files

fez-static.yaml
web_src/layouts/default.html
web_src/root/index.html
web_src/root/[blogs]/2026-01-01-hello-fez.md
web_src/root/[blogs]/2026-01-02-another-post.md
web_src/root/site.css
fez staticbuilds the starter into web_build/ immediately
the generated config doubles as the option reference

fez static build · --watch · --drafts

Build once or on every change

build renders the whole site and reports pages, assets and duration. --watch rebuilds when anything under source_dir or a configured copy source changes; --drafts includes draft: true pages. A failed rebuild prints the error and keeps the last good output.

Built 36 pages and 76 assets in 65ms -> ./demo
Watching ./demo
fez static=fez static build
fez static ../other-site builds a different project root

fez static dev · --port · --host

Watch, serve and reload

dev combines a watcher with a local server and injects a small reload client into HTML responses; every successful rebuild refreshes connected browsers over a WebSocket. --port defaults to 3000 and --host to 127.0.0.1. Clean URLs such as /blog/hello/ resolve to their index.html.

Built 36 pages and 76 assets in 65ms -> ./demo
Serving http://127.0.0.1:4000/
/__fez_static/reload.jsonly while dev runs, never in the build
serve_root and serve_prefix shape the served URL

fez static serve · fez static clean

Serve or remove the existing output

serve serves target_dir as it is, without rebuilding, which is the fastest way to check a production build. clean deletes the target directory and refuses obviously unsafe paths such as the project root.

Serving http://127.0.0.1:3000/

$ fez static clean
Removed ./web_build
no-storeevery response, so reloads always show the current files
HEAD requests and 404s behave like a normal static host

fez static doctor

Validate without publishing

doctor renders into a temporary directory and checks required collection metadata, internal href, src, srcset and fez references, fragment anchors and base_url usage, then throws the directory away. Add data-fez-static-ignore to an element whose target only exists at runtime.

Site is valid: 36 pages and 76 assets

# or, on a broken site
fez static: Static site has 3 problems:
  index.html: missing target /missing/
  index.html: missing anchor #missing
  index.html: missing asset /missing.png
exit 1on any problem, so it fits a CI step
external and protocol URLs are ignored

--help · --info · [site-root]

Everything on one screen

fez static --help prints the commands, options and defaults; --info prints the one-line description used by the fez dispatcher. Inside this repository the same tool runs as ./bin/fez-static.

Usage: fez static [site-root] [options]
       fez static <command> [site-root] [options]

Commands:
  build  dev  serve  clean  doctor  init

Options:
  -h, --help     -w, --watch     --drafts
  -p, --port     --host
bun >= 1.3.8for the native Markdown and YAML support
no additional parser dependency is installed
